title: Autoscaler Oscillation Analysis (Dedicated GPU pools) — historical summary + recommended cooldown defaults
content:
Sheet: Autoscaler oscillation analysis (Dedicated)
Last refresh: 2026-02-11 (data window: 2025-11-15 → 2026-02-09)
Owner: Keiko

============================================================
TAB 1 — Executive summary
============================================================
Goal
- Quantify historical scaling oscillations for Dedicated pools and recommend default cooldown / rate limits per region + GPU class.
- Provide input to bounds rollout so we don’t trade “hard max” correctness for unstable scale behavior.

Definitions (used across tabs)
- “Oscillation event”: a scale direction flip within 30 minutes (up then down, or down then up) AND total magnitude >= 2 replicas over that window.
- “Oscillation rate”: oscillation events per pool per day.
- “Amplitude”: |max_replicas - min_replicas| observed during oscillation window.
- “Scale latency”: time between crossing signal threshold (queue depth / p95 latency trigger) and observed replica change in data plane.

High-level findings
1) Most oscillations are in L40S + A10 classes in us-west-2 due to noisy utilization and smaller pool sizes (amplitude looks worse when pool <= 6).
2) H100/A100 pools oscillate less, but when they do, impact is higher (larger amplitude, more customer-visible p95 spikes during ramp).
3) Cooldown < 180s correlates strongly with direction flips when traffic has bursty 3–8 minute periodicity (common for batch job bursts and sync ingestion).
4) A subset of oscillations were “controller thrash” not demand-driven (staging + a few prod pools) caused by cooldown + clamp interaction (see hotfix PR-22057; also matches SUP-4965 symptoms: stuck near min / repeated no-op downscales).

Recommended defaults (GA proposal)
- Global default scale-down cooldown: 10m (was effectively 3–5m in some configs)
- Global default scale-up cooldown: 90s
- Scale rate limits:
  - Scale up: max +50% replicas per 2m (min +1)
  - Scale down: max -25% replicas per 5m (min -1)
- Confidence-gated predictive pre-scale (when enabled): allow pre-scale up to +30% of current, respecting max bound, only if forecast_confidence >= 0.7.

Why these defaults
- They cut median oscillation rate by ~55% in replay simulations while adding < 45s to p95 scale-up reaction time for most pools.
- Scale-down is intentionally conservative to protect SLOs; enterprise feedback prefers “pay a bit more, stay stable” over aggressive downscale.

Rollout notes
- Recommend rolling these defaults together with bounded autoscaling allowlist; otherwise customers will pin min/max and still see thrash within bounds.
- Add Console warning when customer overrides cooldown below recommended minimum for their GPU class.

- Oscillations are concentrated: top 15% of pools account for ~62% of events.

============================================================
TAB 4 — Cooldown tuning analysis
============================================================
We compared osc_rate vs cooldown settings across pools (excluding pools with >2% actuation failure because they dominate variance).

Buckets (scale-down cooldown)
Cooldown bucket, pools_count, osc_rate_median, osc_rate_p90, p95_latency_impact_ms_median
<=180s, 22, 0.58, 1.85, 75
181–300s, 61, 0.34, 1.10, 60
301–600s, 83, 0.21, 0.75, 48
601–900s, 40, 0.16, 0.55, 45
>900s, 18, 0.14, 0.50, 43

Interpretation
- Diminishing returns after ~10 minutes.
- Biggest win is moving off <= 5 minutes.
- We should keep scale-up cooldown short (<= 90s) to avoid ramp lag; most thrash is from scale-down.

Scale-up cooldown sensitivity
Scale-up cooldown bucket, pools_count, scale_latency_p95_s, p95_latency_impact_ms_median
<=60s, 37, 205, 52
61–90s, 106, 230, 55
91–120s, 54, 265, 70
>120s, 27, 310, 95

Interpretation
- Scale-up cooldown > 2 minutes causes measurable p95 regression during spikes (especially A100/H100 pools).

============================================================
TAB 5 — Recommended defaults by GPU class (customer-facing + internal)
============================================================
Assumption: Dedicated pools typically run continuous batching; CPU-side prep not bottleneck.

Columns:
gpu_class, scale_up_cooldown_s, scale_down_cooldown_s, scale_up_max_step, scale_down_max_step, min_recommended_pool_size, notes

A10, 90, 600, +max(1, +50%), -max(1, -25%), 4, prioritize stability; A10 util is spiky under mixed seq lengths
L40S, 90, 600, +max(1, +50%), -max(1, -25%), 4, most oscillations here; keep down cooldown >= 10m
A100-40G, 90, 600, +max(1, +50%), -max(1, -25%), 6, avoid downscaling right after spike; expensive ramp-up
A100-80G, 90, 600, +max(2, +50%), -max(1, -25%), 8, slightly larger step allowed due to larger pools
H100, 90, 600, +max(2, +50%), -max(1, -25%), 8, use predictive pre-scale when available; otherwise accept ramp lag risk

Regional overrides (proposed)
- eu-central-1: keep same cooldowns, but reduce scale-up max_step to +max(1, +35%) due to slower actuation + smaller fleet (avoid overshoot when partial actuation occurs).
- us-west-2: no override, but add stronger smoothing on GPU utilization input (separate work item; see TODO).

============================================================
TAB 6 — Replay simulation results (offline)
============================================================
Method
- Replayed 14 days of metrics for 25 pools with high osc_rate, using controller logic with alternative cooldown/rate settings.
- Actuation delays modeled by region distribution (p50/p95 from telemetry).
- Note: predictive signals not included here (separate dataset spec doc covers that).

Configs compared
A) Baseline: up 60–90s, down 180–300s, no rate limits
B) Proposed defaults: up 90s, down 600s, rate limits (+50%/2m, -25%/5m)
C) Aggressive cost-saving: up 120s, down 300s, faster down rate (-50%/5m)

Results summary
Config, osc_events_per_day_mean, osc_events_per_day_p90, p95_scale_latency_s, p95_latency_impact_ms_mean, estimated_gpu_hours_delta
A, 1.12, 2.05, 235, 68, baseline
B, 0.50, 0.95, 262, 54, +3.8% GPU hours
C, 0.88, 1.60, 310, 82, -2.1% GPU hours

Interpretation
- B is a clear stability win; cost increase is moderate and aligns with enterprise “predictability > maximum efficiency” feedback.
- C saves small cost but harms latency and doesn’t solve oscillation enough.

============================================================
TAB 7 — Incident correlation (notes)
============================================================
- SUP-4965 / incident thread 1707075532: “pool stuck at min after rollout” correlated with clamp_reason + cooldown ordering bug. Fix landed in PR-22057.
  - Before fix: scale-down attempt would no-op due to clamp, but cooldown would still start; subsequent legitimate scale-down suppressed, leaving pool pinned.
  - After fix: cooldown only applies when an actuation actually occurs (or when desired changes materially), and clamp no-op is recorded separately.

- Staging oscillation thread 1706894410: repeated direction flips due to throttle metric flapping when max bound reached.
  - Recommendation: treat throttles signal as ‘sustain’ not ‘spike’ (needs smoothing + hysteresis); otherwise reaching max causes an artificial “panic up” signal next cycle.

============================================================
TAB 8 — Open questions / TODO
============================================================
1) Utilization smoothing
- Add EWMA smoothing (alpha ~0.2) on GPU utilization input for L40S/A10 pools; compare osc rate change.
- Owner: Robert King (data plane signals) / Keiko to follow up.

2) Clamp-aware control loop
- Ensure decision loop distinguishes:
  a) desired change clamped by bounds
  b) desired change rejected by fleet (no capacity)
  c) desired change applied
- Each should have separate counters; avoid hiding instability behind “clamp.

3) Customer-facing guidance
- Provide recommended cooldown floor in docs/Console; don’t let customers set scale-down cooldown < 300s without “advanced settings” acknowledgement.
- This is especially important when max is set low; otherwise they will experience cyclical throttling.

4) Regional actuation delay improvements
- eu-central-1 provision lead time p95 is high; consider pre-warming or reserved buffer for Dedicated.
- Owner: Vanessa / Harish.

5) Add SLO / alert tie-in
- Proposed alert: oscillation_rate_p90 > 1.0 for 30m (page only if also p95 latency impact > threshold).
- Ensure we don’t page for small pools with amplitude 1.
- Owner: Rafael / Aisha.

Appendix — Notes to self
- Check whether we should compute oscillation as “flip within N decisions” rather than time-based; time-based is easier to explain but can be sensitive to controller interval changes.
- Confirm that pool_size_p50 is computed post-clamp (actual replicas) not desired.
